entries.label: Legal, title, inspection and other closing fees (planner default)
entries.notes: ASSUMPTION, editable in the planner. $2,500 is the fee line the down-payment planner spec itemizes in its Example A (audit addendum 2026-09-30, item 2: $4,475 net LTT + $1,808 PST on premium + ~$2,500 fees). Audit addendum A quotes an itemized cash target of ~$44,500 for Example A, which implies ~$3,200 of fees instead; the two could not be reconciled because the spec and research files were not readable in the build session. Re-check against down-payment-planner-research.md before publish.
entries.source: hidden_files/down-payment-planner-calculator-spec.md (section 5, Example A line items, as restated by the 2026-09-30 audit addendum)
entries.source_note: Spec design default, not a government figure.

entries.label: Extra cash cushion on top of itemized closing costs (planner default)
entries.notes: ASSUMPTION. Default $0 so the planner shows only itemized costs. The spec's Example A used a ~$15,000 closing figure (later a $50,000 target) that bakes in roughly $6,000 of cushion no source supports (audit addendum A). The UI shows this as an editable, labeled assumption.
entries.source_note: Design default, not a sourced figure.

entries.label: Planner default savings interest rate
entries.notes: ASSUMPTION, re-check. 2.75% is the spec default. Per eq.account_rates.2026_09 (bank-promos.json, checked 2026-09-28), EQ Bank's 2.75% requires $2,000/mo in direct deposits; the base rate is 1.00%. Shown in the assumptions panel as 're-check'.
entries.source_note: Spec default; conditional-rate caveat from bank-promos.json eq.account_rates.2026_09.

entries.label: Illustrative mortgage contract rate (planner default)
entries.notes: ASSUMPTION: illustrative, verify. Taken from the affordability spec's worked example, not market data. Qualifying rate = max(contract + 2 points, 5.25%) = 6.50% (osfi.mqr.2026).
entries.source_note: Illustrative design default, not a quoted market rate.

entries.label: Best 5-year fixed rate snapshot (Ratehub, Sept 2026)
entries.notes: SNAPSHOT, expires 2026-10-15. Mirrors mortgage.rates_snapshot.2026_09 in mortgage-2026.json so the planner can cite it with its own expiry. Shown alongside the illustrative 4.50% default, never instead of a fresh quote.

entries.label: Tax refund from an $8,000 FHSA deduction, Ontario illustrative range
entries.notes: Per 2026-09-30 audit addendum item 10 (corrects the spec's $1,300 to $3,400). Reproduces as $8,000 x 19.05% (14% federal + 5.05% ON, lowest brackets) = $1,524 and $8,000 x 43.41% (26% federal + 11.16% ON x 1.56 surtax) = $3,473. Not the maximum: at the top ON combined rate (53.53%) the refund would be about $4,282.
entries.source: federal-brackets-2026.json + provincial-brackets-2026.json + on.surtax.2026 (derived); range per 2026-09-30 audit addendum
entries.source_note: Derived from verified 2026 bracket figures; range endpoints chosen by the spec audit.

entries.label: HBP extended repayment grace for 2026-2028 withdrawals (DISPUTED)
entries.notes: DISPUTED, do not present as settled law. hbp-research.md says CRA shows a 5-year grace in effect for first withdrawals made Jan 1, 2026 to Dec 31, 2028 (repayments would start the 5th year after withdrawal instead of the 2nd); fhsa-hbp-2026.json hbp.repayment_start says do not encode until confirmed as legislated. The planner shows it only as a second schedule labeled 'confirm before relying on it'.
entries.source_note: Spring Economic Update 2026 description; legislative status unconfirmed.

entries.label: Home insurance per month (planner default)
entries.notes: ASSUMPTION: midpoint of the $100 to $200/mo design range in rent_vs_buy.assumptions (rent-housing-2026.json). Editable in the planner.
entries.source_note: Design default, not a sourced figure.
